description: Raise the SLSQP iteration cap MAX_ITER from 200 to 500 so each random-restart attempt can converge further.
Replace the shrink-only repair with a gradient-style relaxation that pushes overlapping centres apart (clipped to the square) before the existing radius shrink, and return the moved centres.

Replace the shrink-only repair with a velocity-based push: overlapping circles get a decaying velocity along their overlap direction, their centres move, and the touching pair is then shrunk, with the moved centres returned to solve.
Make the repair shrink amount proportional to each pairwise overlap by subtracting half the overlap (plus the SHRINK margin) from both radii instead of scaling them multiplicatively.

After the SLSQP random restarts pick the best packing, run a short simulated-annealing pass that moves one random circle at a time, resets its radius to the largest feasible value, and keeps the best state seen.

Initialise each SLSQP restart's circle centres from a scrambled Sobol sequence (scipy.stats.qmc, seeded from the run rng) scaled into [INIT_LOW, 1-INIT_LOW], instead of uniform random points, so the starts cover the square more evenly.

Stop each SLSQP restart early once its radius sum gains less than 1e-4 over 10 iterations (after 20 iterations), keeping the last iterate and restarting with the next random start, so the time budget goes to more restarts; the optional extension of runs that converge fast is left out to keep the edit minimal.

Start half of the SLSQP restarts from a hexagonal lattice (choosing n of its points at random and adding small Gaussian jitter) and the other half from uniform random centres, so the optimizer still explores from varied starts.

Start half of the SLSQP restarts from a hexagonal lattice (choosing n of its points at random and adding small Gaussian jitter) and the other half from uniform random centres, so the optimizer still explores from varied starts.
Add a quadratic penalty on constraint violations (box, overlap, and radius bounds) to the SLSQP objective in _solve_once, while keeping the hard constraints.
Aborted the Newton-Raphson repair idea: it is another repair-step variant, and repair variants have already been tried three times without gain.

Replace the SLSQP local solver with L-BFGS-B over box-bounded centres and radii, using an analytic gradient and an increasing quadratic penalty for overlap and wall violations, then keep the existing repair step.

Replace the SLSQP local solver with L-BFGS-B over box-bounded centres and radii, using an analytic gradient and an increasing quadratic penalty for overlap and wall violations, then keep the existing repair step.
Extend the existing continuation schedule of overlap-penalty weights from 1e5 to 1e6 so the final L-BFGS-B stage uses the very high Omega the spec asks for.
Draw initial radii from a capped heavy-tailed (Pareto) distribution, so most starts have small circles and a few have larger ones, instead of a fixed 0.05 for every circle.
Recursively re-apply the overlap repair with a smaller shrink factor at each level until no overlaps remain.
Start each L-BFGS-B restart from a jittered hexagonal grid, choosing n of its points at random, instead of uniform random centres.

Skip the iterative-projection repair idea: its centre-projection step already happens (solve clips centres to [0,1] and L-BFGS-B enforces the box bounds), and repair variants have not helped in four earlier tries.

After the penalty continuation in _solve_once, perturb the radii by about 2% and re-run L-BFGS-B at the final penalty weight for three rounds, keeping each perturbed result only if its penalized objective improves.
Replace the shrink-only overlap repair with a Newton-Raphson step on pairwise overlap distances, with a line search that keeps the packing from getting worse.
Abort the Recursive Repair idea: it is another variant of the overlap repair step, and repair variants have been rejected in four prior slots.
Scale the pairwise overlap penalty by a new OVERLAP_W = 3.0 weight relative to the wall penalty, so the L-BFGS-B continuation pushes harder against overlaps before the repair step.
Sequential optimisation: before the final 1e5 penalty stage in _solve_once, freeze the largest third of the circles at their current positions and radii, so only the smaller circles are re-optimised.

issues: Integrity is fine. The diff adds no file or network access, pastes no coordinates and uses no test labels. All new randomness comes from the seeded rng.

Likely design flaw, not a veto: each step calls _repair(nc, cur_r.copy()), starting from the current radii. In the starting script, _repair only shrinks radii. If that still holds, the sum of radii can never go up, so delta <= 0 every time and best_r stays the input packing. The annealing would then spend 10% of the time without being able to improve anything. The result is still valid, but the gain should be about zero. A single run of -2.6315 against -2.6321 fits that.

Time check: the restart loop stops at about 80% of time_limit and the annealing adds 10% (3 s), so a call takes about 27 s plus any overshoot from the last SLSQP run. That is well under the 45 s limit.

Validity check: the packing returned is either the incumbent's best, which has already been repaired, or the output of _repair on clipped centres. Both go through the same check as the incumbent, so I see no crash risk beyond the incumbent's own.

z check: I recomputed z = (-2.6321 - (-2.6315)) / (0.0023 * sqrt(1/1 + 1/2)) ≈ -0.0006 / 0.00282 ≈ -0.21. This matches the harness's -0.220 within rounding. The candidate is slightly worse, though not significantly, so rejecting is right. The comparison rests on only 1 candidate run and 2 incumbent runs.

description: After the random restarts, run a 3-second simulated-annealing phase on the best packing that perturbs the centres with a cooling step size and temperature, repairs the radii with the existing validity-preserving repair, and keeps the best valid packing found.

Replace the random starting layout in each restart with a greedy sequential placement: each circle goes to the best of 400 random candidate points, at the largest radius that fits without overlap, before the existing L-BFGS-B penalty continuation settles the packing.

Initialise each restart's centres on a jittered grid (ceil(sqrt(n))^2 cell centres, n of them chosen at random with the seeded rng) and start all radii at a small common value of 0.02, instead of uniform random centres and radii 0.05.

Adds a final polish of the best packing found by the random restarts: one extra L-BFGS-B run from it with 5x the iteration cap, repaired, and kept only if its radius sum is larger (a partial, minimal version of the adaptive-time idea).

Add a successive-convex-approximation polish after each restart: linearise each centre distance, solve an LP for centres and radii within a shrinking trust region, and keep a step only if its repaired radius sum improves.
Add a force-directed untangling pass that moves centres away from overlapping neighbours for a fixed number of steps before the penalty continuation in each L-BFGS-B restart.
Entropy-based radius initialization: draw initial radii from a high-variance, large-circle-favouring distribution instead of the fixed INIT_RADIUS.

Basin-hopping local search: every second iteration, perturb the best packing's centres and radii with small Gaussian noise and re-settle it with L-BFGS-B at the high penalty weights (1e4, 1e5) instead of starting from a fresh random layout.

issues: No sign of getting around the measurement: no file or network access, no pasted coordinates, no use of labels. The change only adds alternating block-coordinate L-BFGS-B passes: radii are solved with centres fixed, then centres with radii fixed.
No bug found that would make the result meaningless. L-BFGS-B accepts equal lower and upper bounds as fixed variables. The existing repair step still guarantees a valid packing.

Possible no-op: `if lam == 1e4` compares floats exactly. If the code builds lam by repeated multiplication instead of taking it from a literal list, the new block may never run, so it would never be tested. Worth checking in the full file.
The extra minimize calls in each restart reduce the number of restarts that fit in the time budget. This trade-off may explain the slightly worse result.

Recomputed z: the candidate's loss is 0.0006 worse (-2.6315 vs -2.6321). The standard error is 0.0023*sqrt(1/1+1/2) ≈ 0.00282, so |z| ≈ 0.21 against the reported -0.221. The small gap is probably from rounding the inputs. Both say there is no significant difference, and reject is the right call.
There is only one candidate run, so the evidence is weak either way. Still, no claim goes beyond what the numbers show.
